flag_summary: An early two-control Claybridge fuzz box is documented before the named Fuzzmaster. Treat as a distinct pre-Fuzzmaster production state pending full chronology.
Surviving Claybridge research distinguishes the original Fuzzmaster from later Wildcat and MKIV states; control count, enclosure geometry and transistor populations differ across surviving specimens.
Wildcat is a distinct named production state with different enclosure proportions, faceplate treatment, knobs and BC109 transistor implementation compared with the earlier green Fuzzmaster and MKIV.
MKIV is a distinct named state in the surviving Fuzzmaster sequence. Existing research indicates it is related to, but not identical with, earlier Claybridge fuzz states.

A surviving early amp-top Fuzz Blender lacks the MKIV designation and uses a different physical format from the later MKIV stompbox. Whether it represents V1, an earlier family member, or another product state remains unresolved.
The MKIV designation implies earlier revisions may have existed, and historical research explicitly raises the unresolved possibility of MKII and MKIII. No complete sequence is currently established.

The FZ-1 family crosses documented production contexts and later revisions. Existing census work already separates FZ-1, FZ-1A and FZ-1B; specimen-level differences should be logged before collapsing early units into one visual state.

Surviving Nu-Fuzz specimens show Sierra/Rosac branding transitions, different module versus eyelet-board construction, and differing knob/logo treatments. These may represent transitional production states rather than simple cosmetic options.

Early Rosac ads identify multiple related products and surviving examples show the same Sierra-labeled Sprague module supply issue seen in Nu-Fuzz. Treat as a cross-model production-transition flag, not yet separate generations.

Zonk Machine and Zonk Machine II are already distinct catalog records. Additional specimen-level enclosure and production differences should be examined before treating all Zonk Machine examples as one state.
